title: The Shindes of Gwalior
subtitle: Scindia: from Bajirao's commander to rulers of north India · 1731 – 1948
subject: gwalior-state
intro: The Shinde (Scindia) family rose from service under Peshwa Bajirao I to become the most powerful house of the Maratha confederacy. Under Mahadji Shinde they controlled Delhi and the Mughal emperor; after defeat by the British in 1803 they ruled Gwalior as the largest princely state of central India until 1948.

members.note: Dattaji Shinde leads the army until 1760; Jankoji is executed after Panipat

members.name: Disputed succession
members.note: Kedarji and Manaji Shinde contest the headship
Daulatrao's widow Baiza Bai is regent until 1833

events.title: Setback at Lalsot
events.summary: Rajput armies and deserting Mughal troops defeat Mahadji at Lalsot; he rebuilds his army around de Boigne's brigades.

events.title: Mahadji retakes Delhi
events.summary: Mahadji's troops drive out Ghulam Qadir, who had blinded Shah Alam II, and restore the emperor.

events.title: Patan and Merta
events.summary: De Boigne's brigades crush Ismail Beg and the Rajputs at Patan in June and at Merta in September.

events.title: Mahadji comes to Pune
events.summary: Mahadji returns to Pune at the height of his power, rivalling Nana Phadnavis at the Peshwa's court.

events.title: Holkar defeated at Lakheri
events.summary: Shinde's brigades rout Tukoji Holkar's army at Lakheri, the deepest split yet in the confederacy.

events.title: British control after Maharajpur
events.summary: After the defeats at Maharajpur and Panniar the Gwalior army is cut down and a council of regency works under the British Resident.

events.title: Jiwajirao succeeds
events.summary: Madho Rao Scindia dies; his son Jiwajirao becomes the last ruling Maharaja of Gwalior.

events.title: Ranoji Shinde settles at Ujjain
events.summary: Bajirao divides the revenue of Malwa among his commanders. Ranoji Shinde, who began as a personal attendant of the Peshwa, makes Ujjain his base — the start of the Shinde state.

events.title: Ranoji dies; Jayappa succeeds
events.summary: Ranoji dies on campaign. His son Jayappa takes over, with his brother Dattaji as a leading commander.

events.title: Jayappa assassinated in Marwar
events.summary: While intervening in a succession dispute in Marwar, Jayappa is murdered at Nagaur. His young son Jankoji succeeds, with Dattaji as guardian.

events.title: Dattaji Shinde killed at Burari Ghat
events.summary: Defending the north against Ahmad Shah Abdali, Dattaji is killed near Delhi.

events.title: Panipat: Jankoji executed, Mahadji crippled
events.summary: At the Third Battle of Panipat the young Jankoji Shinde is captured and executed. Mahadji Shinde escapes with a wound that leaves him lame.

events.title: Mahadji Shinde takes charge
events.summary: After years of disputed succession, Mahadji — Ranoji's youngest son — is recognised as head of the family.

events.title: Back in Delhi with Shah Alam II
events.summary: Mahadji is among the leaders of the army that restores the exiled emperor Shah Alam II to Delhi.

events.title: Victory at Wadgaon
events.summary: Mahadji's forces surround a British army marching on Pune, forcing the Convention of Wadgaon.

events.title: Treaty of Salbai
events.summary: Mahadji negotiates the peace ending the First Anglo-Maratha War; the British recognise him as an independent power in the north.

events.title: Regent of the Mughal empire
events.summary: Shah Alam II makes Mahadji his Vakil-ul-Mutlaq. The Shindes now control Delhi and the person of the emperor.

events.title: De Boigne's brigades
events.summary: Mahadji's European-trained infantry under Benoît de Boigne win at Patan and Merta, making the Shinde army the strongest in north India.

events.title: Mahadji dies near Pune
events.summary: Mahadji dies at Wanavdi near Pune. His grand-nephew Daulatrao, about 15, inherits the army and lands.

events.title: Assaye and Laswari
events.summary: In the Second Anglo-Maratha War Daulatrao's armies are defeated by Arthur Wellesley at Assaye and by Gerard Lake at Delhi and Laswari.

events.title: Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon
events.summary: Daulatrao cedes Delhi, Agra and his territories north of the Jumna and in Gujarat to the Company.

events.title: Capital at Gwalior
events.summary: Daulatrao's camp (lashkar) below Gwalior fort becomes the permanent capital of the state.

events.title: Neutral in the last war
events.summary: Under a new treaty Daulatrao stays out of the Third Anglo-Maratha War; the Shinde state survives under British protection while the Peshwa falls.

events.title: Baiza Bai's regency
events.summary: After Daulatrao's death his widow Baiza Bai rules as regent for the adopted heir Jankoji II until she is pushed out in 1833.

events.title: Maharajpur and Panniar
events.summary: After a succession crisis the British invade. The Gwalior army is defeated in two battles on the same day; the state's army is reduced and placed under British supervision.

events.title: Rani Lakshmibai and Tatya Tope at Gwalior
events.summary: During the revolt of 1857 Rani Lakshmibai and Tatya Tope seize Gwalior; Jayajirao flees to Agra. Lakshmibai is killed fighting nearby on 18 June and the British retake the city.

events.title: Jai Vilas Mahal
events.summary: Jayajirao builds the Jai Vilas palace in Gwalior in a European style.

events.title: Merger into Madhya Bharat
events.summary: Gwalior joins neighbouring states to form Madhya Bharat; Jiwajirao Scindia becomes its Rajpramukh (governor) until 1956.
